deep_dive.title: PACT: Plan-Action Consistency Training by Preserving Correct Plans and Repairing Actions in GUI Agents
deep_dive.abstract: GUI agents can formulate a correct immediate plan in their reasoning yet emit an action that fails to execute it, creating an execution gap. This recurring mismatch undermines reliable task completion, as a single execution error can derail a multi-step workflow. In outcome-supervised reinforcement learning, broadcasting a negative response-level advantage across all generated tokens risks penalizing valid planning together with erroneous execution. To address this credit-assignment conflict, we introduce PACT (Plan-Action Consistency Training), a training framework that combines reference-aligned plan protection and plan-aligned action repair without altering the original scalar action reward. Using annotated reference actions to identify execution gaps, PACT protects the verified plan by masking negative policy-gradient contributions across its token span. Keeping the generated reasoning unchanged as context, it then favors the reference action over the emitted erroneous action through a preference surrogate with stop-gradient pair weights. Compared with the outcome-only baseline, PACT raises AndroidWorld task success from 60.34% to 68.97% (+8.63 pp), while improving rule-based plan-action consistency on AndroidControl High from 83.71% to 89.74% (+6.03 pp). Adapting PACT to desktop agents also improves task success from 40.92% to 44.17% (+3.25 pp) on the full 369-task OSWorld benchmark. Together, these results establish PACT as an effective credit-assignment framework for bridging execution gaps and improving task completion across mobile and desktop GUI environments.

deep_dive.llm_tldr_en: GUI agents often produce a correct plan but an unexecutable action. PACT adds reference-aligned plan protection and plan-aligned action repair under outcome-supervised RL, fixing credit assignment without changing the scalar action reward.
deep_dive.llm_tldr_cn: GUI智能体在推理中常能给出正确的即时计划，却输出无法执行的动作，形成计划与执行之间的鸿沟，单步失误即可导致多步任务失败。本文提出PACT训练框架，在结果监督强化学习下加入参考对齐的计划保护与计划对齐的动作修复，避免负向优势被广播到所有token而误伤正确计划。方法不改变原有标量动作奖励，用标注参考引导信用分配。该框架显著缓解计划-动作不一致问题，提升GUI智能体多步任务的可靠完成率。

quick_skim.title: ATLAS-Finance: Benchmarking AI Agents in Realistic Banking Environments
quick_skim.abstract: Professional work involves under-specified assignments, where relevant information is spread across workplace applications and may conflict or change over time. To evaluate how well frontier agents can perform economically valuable work in such settings, we introduce ATLAS-Finance, a benchmark of 100 end-to-end investment-banking tasks across 13 simulated firms. As in real banking workflows, agents must search email, chat, calendars, notes, and files to identify requirements, gather information, reconcile conflicts/updates, and then build complex financial models. Tasks were developed by experienced bankers based on their real deal work and take them 15-30 hours to complete. Agent deliverables are evaluated with expert-authored rubrics (median: 124.5 criteria) covering financial rationale and results, spreadsheet construction, completeness, and formatting. Despite completing substantial portions of the requested work, current agents rarely produce correct deliverables. Across today's frontier models, the best ones (Claude Opus and Fable) pass fewer than 11% of tasks.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: Frontier agents must handle under-specified professional work spanning many applications; ATLAS-Finance offers 100 investment-banking tasks across 13 simulated firms, scored by expert rubrics, to measure realistic cross-application agent performance.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 现实专业工作往往需求模糊、信息分散在多个应用并会冲突变化，现有评测难以衡量前沿智能体的真实能力。作者提出ATLAS-Finance基准，包含13家模拟公司中的100个端到端投资银行任务，要求智能体检索邮件、聊天、日历与文件并构建财务模型。任务由资深银行家依据真实交易设计，采用专家撰写量规评估交付物。该基准为跨应用多步计算机使用智能体的评测提供了贴近真实工作流的协议。
